a.text: Eulogy—
I've been going with this two-hundred-odd Leithanian refugee group for...
I can't even tell how many days it's been.
At Leithanien's border region, Catastrophe brought about an earthquake, which in turn caused the river to breach its levee.
These poor people lost their home, sought shelter somewhere higher on instinct, and fled all the way here.
The winter days are looming, and many are ill. We're stuck in place.
We have only temporary shelters cobbled together with wood, open to the elements, until help comes for us.
We're currently in Victoria's northwest, near the mountains of Kjerag, far removed from any cities.
As cold weather approaches, our food is running bare. No clothing that can keep us warm, and all medicine has been used up.
Eulogy... this operation turned out nothing like I thought. How could it be so arduous, so tough... Where are the humanitarians, the philanthropic barons...
Dad...
We're still trying, but... so many of us are slowly dying... I'm stood in all this passing away, and I can't see the light.

steps.text: Victorian northwest border region, somewhere in the forests

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (I can't shake this feeling someone's been tailing me the whole time.)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (Heheh, don't look away now!)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ah! These are the footprints of—!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: An omnivorous beast! The teeth are in fairly shabby shape. But its claws are sharp; chances are, it tears its prey to slivers before it eats.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It shouldn't ordinarily attack people, but supposing food runs low in winter... they might just start picking off human stragglers...
Aaaah!
Ah, wh-whah, wha-wha-aaaaaah—!
Grace—!!!
Buh, bah, whaaaah, don't leave me all alone!!!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So it was you, Rita. Get over here, quickly.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Grace, Grace!! There was rustling in those bushes over there!! It's a beast! Is this where we're going to die?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hahaha! Don't lose your head, I made all that up on the spot.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I was just curious who was creeping around behind me, and here you are.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mmph!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Come on, Grace, don't scare me like that!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Well, I might've made up the beasts, but people who secretly follow you are plenty dangerous too.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Now, confess. Why are you tracking me?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I—I was hungry.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You were hungry, so you followed me looking for food? I don't know, you seem pretty chipper to me, don't you?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mama and Papa don't have anything to eat. They gave their last bit of food to me...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: How about the harvest group's food?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mama got ill forever ago. After Papa got hurt hunting, the harvest group all said our family doesn't work for anything, and they don't want to give us food...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: And they said, it's winter now, and they can barely find any food like this. There's not enough stores in camp, and unless it gets warmer, we'll be more and more short on food.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (That's true enough. The situation's continued to deteriorate.)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (If help still doesn't show up, then when the time comes...)

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: And... even if I went with them, I don't have any contribution to make to the hunt. They just won't share anything with me. So the last few days, I haven't gone with them...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Is that how they're going to be now?!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: *whimper*... Both Mama and Papa are sleeping on sickbeds, and it's cold, and I can't eat enough to not be hungry. I don't feel good.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Grace, can you help tell me which things are edible? I want to pick some stuff before I go back...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Even just some weeds would be okay. It doesn't matter how bad it tastes, either. As long as I can feel fuller, it's fine!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: No problem, leave it to me! But just eating weeds you find on the wayside won't do it. If you really want to be full, you'll want beast meat too.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The food you ultimately get from scrabbling around here won't be enough in the long-term, versus the effort you spend.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: But I—I can't catch beasts.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Mmm... leave that for today, then. Emergencies first. Tomorrow, I'll take you up north, and we'll see if we can't catch a few little beasties for ourselves!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Really? Thank you, Grace!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: This is great! Mama and Papa can eat properly too!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Save your thanks just for now. In exchange, listen to what I say today, and don't go scarpering off, got it?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Oh, careful where you're stepping! Don't you trip over.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Are we looking for herbs we can eat now? Mama and Papa are waiting for me to bring back food!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Ah, this one looks like a herb! Grace, is this one edible?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hm... it might look very much like you could eat it, but it's actually poisonous.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Um, then what about this one here?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Not that one either. It's too tough to chew, and you'll make your mouth bleed.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Then this one! It's a fruit! It's fresh, too. Is this one okay?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: This is a cysteye. A berry that looks just like a cystybeast's eye, right?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But it's not edible. It looks plenty delicious, and it's sweet if you try it too. But, afterwards, it'll give you tremendous tummy problems, and the more you eat, the worse it'll get.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Some Victorian nobles use them as weight-loss drugs, run themselves dry eating them, then their lowered immunity leads to all sorts of illness... no matter if it fills you, it's awful for the human body.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Giving other species the runs to spread its own seeds. Evolution truly goes in funny ways, sometimes.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: *whimper*—What do we do then?! We can't find anything to eat at all.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Don't lose heart. The fruit might not be edible, but you can eat its leaves. They're a little bitter, but won't do any damage to the body. Boiling them will help take some of the edge off.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Then I'll pick just a few leaves to try.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Heheh, I'll say your luck's not too bad! Look at what I'm holding—you can go find a few of these too.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Are those pebbles?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Look on top of them. These are wild mossoats—these spores here look just like oats, that's why. You can eat these.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The books said some of Ursus's farming peasantry in the Northern Tundra grow these, but I never imagined we'd find some here too.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: That's superb! I'll go pick some too!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The more, the better. Pull off the husks, wash them, and you can boil them for a thin porridge.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: But if we pick them all now, won't there be no more left later?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The mossoat harvest cycle goes by in a flash. After the harvest period, its sugar content gets absorbed, the spores on top are formed, the 'oat' part of it withers some, and it turns bitter and inedible.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Then are these ones right now good mossoats?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: They are! You've got sound luck, Rita! But these are wild ones after all—they won't be plenty. You'll want to pick all of these to have enough for a full pot.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I'll go for it, then!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Incredible stuff, Rita. I'll help you out too.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Thank you, Grace! Hehe, I'm gonna pick loads, and then I'll hide them all, and only give them to Mama and Papa!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Once I pick all the mossoats, I'll come pick the medicine herbs with you, Grace!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Perfect. You look around this flat area, then, and don't go too far. I'll see what's westwards. If anything happens, just shout for me!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mm-hm! I got it, Grace!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (It's raining...)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (Brrr. The stones are starting to get slippery, too.)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (About time I go back and check on Rita.)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ritaaaaa—!!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Iiii'm—oooo—veeer—heeeere—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (Why is she so far away?)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita?? Where are you??

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Iiii'm—dooown—heeeere—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Huh?!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Iiiii—wasn't—caaareful—and—Iiiii—sliiipped—dooown—heeeree—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Are you hurt?!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Don't move about! I'll be down in a flash!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Graaace—beeee—caaaare—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Aaaaagh—!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Ah! I wanted to tell you it was really slippery over there, so careful not to step on the stones and fall down here too.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What does this pit think it is, a slide?!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Hahaha, there's grass growing from your head now!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Oh? How about you join in with me? Hupsie-daisy!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Aha! A moustache!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Achoo! Ah—ah—achoo! *whimper*... You got all the leafy stuff stuck in my nose, Grace. It's itchy.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Pff! Watch your snot—you've got snot coming out!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Nnn...

steps.name: Grace & Rita
steps.text: Hahahahahahahahahahaha!!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Alright, I'm done picking on you. Anyhow, what have you been doing down here?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I couldn't find more mossoats up above, so I went to see if there were any underground, so I could pick even more.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: And then I wasn't careful and I fell!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Are you hurt?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I landed on my butt a little hard, but everything else is okay.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Phew. Thank goodness for that.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Weren't you supposed to be listening to me? I never told you to come anywhere like this, did I?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: But I only have enough for one pot, and it's not that much. Besides, if we went harvesting tomorrow and it was too late, wouldn't they all be wasted?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You still have to mind your own safety, though.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mm-hm... I left my basket up above, so it's alright!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I saw it just now. Which is why I left my basket there too.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Next to mine?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Yep, all snuggly.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Hehehe, that's really nice.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It's raining now. Here, put this on you. Don't catch a cold now.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: This leaf is huge!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I picked it just before. Wear it on your head, put your horns through these two holes, and that'll block the rain.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: My ears are chilly. I feel a little bad.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Don't you take it off. The rain'll love to give you a cold if it soaks you. If you get ill too, who's going to care for your mum and dad?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: That's right, I'm our provider now! I have to make sure Mama and Papa are well-fed!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Grace, aren't you gonna put on a leaf?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You wear yours for now.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I've actually barely ever gotten rain-soaked. Feels a little unlike anything else.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: How come—how come you never got wet in the rain before?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Maybe Victoria doesn't get that much rain, actually?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rain's a very common sight in Victoria, to be clear, but it's true—I've never been able to shower in it.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Especially like now. Nothing between me and the final rains of autumn, pattering on my head...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Then I'm even stronger than you are! When it's raining, I fetch laundry outside all the time, and do farm work.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Rain is pretty much like when the village headman got mad at me. He went, Rita, pbphth, whatbth is phthe meaning of thisph thbphruckus—!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hahahaha! Oh, that headman. Just like a spit sprinkler when worked up.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: But he can't sprinkle anymore now...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: He'd just gotten too old. Too tired, too.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I saw it. That day I secretly followed you, and saw you carrying him out on your back, and you were really struggling to take him so far away, and then soon after you put him down, he just...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Just floated away like ash, like when we burn wood...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Will my Mama and Papa become like that too?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It's been two weeks already since the distress team left. Given they're following my map, they should've found a nearby town by now.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Besides, I've picked so much medicine today, and you've picked plenty of food too. Your mum and dad will be just fine!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Right! I've worked really hard! Mama and Papa are gonna be better for sure!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: By the way, Grace, why don't you let anyone else help you pick medicine?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Mm... you know, everyone's in the same boat as your family. They can't eat their fill now, so securing food is more or less top priority for them all.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: That's why nobody has a hand to lend, see.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The rain's getting stronger, it looks like. Your mum and dad will be worried about you. Head on back first, okay? I can find the rest of the herbs we need by myself.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mm-hm! I need to bring back everything I picked. I bet Mama and Papa are just as hungry.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Can you still tell the way back?

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Of course I can!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Then I'll lift you up out of here. Careful, now.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hnph!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: I'm out!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Grace, grab my hand now, I'll pull you up!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hahaha, I'm miles heavier than you are! I can climb out by myself! Don't worry about me, hurry back and check in on your mum and dad!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Alright~

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Don't run too fast! Watch your step!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Alriiight—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hm... and now we worry about what I'm doing.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I just saw the herbs I needed on the cliff over there.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The rain's not going to make this tunnel hard for me, but am I still going to make it up that cliff?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Yowch, I must've gashed that ankle when I fell down. The wound's fairly big. Need something to stop the bleeding first.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But I'm not going to win at any gymnastics once I'm bound up. That makes the cliff even harder.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: *hiss*! God, my ankle hurts... I'm feeling a little dizzy too. Have I gotten fatigued lately?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita's mum's in terrible shape. Her dad's suffered external wounds, and I gave first-aid treatment, but it's still at risk of infection.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The nobles couldn't have possibly missed refugees entering their estate, so why are they so unconcerned... not even just to deport them... why haven't they shown up?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The refugees long since ran out of pharmaceuticals, and now all they have is plant remedies for simple treatment. I need to pick more. I need to be able to help more!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I hope to heaven we can last until the distress team comes back with someone. I hope to heaven...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ah, I can't get bogged down in this. If I let the rain get any worse, that cliff'll only be harder! I need to hurry and pick what I need! I'll bandage myself after I'm back down!
Victorian northwest border region, refugee camp

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Fever medicine for the Hanses. This much should do the trick...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Toothache painkillers for Peter, but the pain is all it kills... these few herbals might not be quite enough.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Bug repellant... ugh, why am I missing something! Hunger must've shook it out of my mind. I'll go back outside to search later... it's already dark now, and the rain's not dying down...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Huh? Why's someone at the entrance to my room?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Miss Arizona!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Miss Arizona!!!!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'm coming! I'm right here!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Miss Arizona, where on Terra were you?! Some—Someone's gotten extremely sick, out of nowhere!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: (It can't be another case like the village headman, can it?)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Where? Show me to them!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Here. Right in here.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: This room is...?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita's family's?!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita? Are you doing alright?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: No reaction... palms severely scalded, contusions on arms, swelling on the back of the head. Nnn... and a slight fever. She was so well before, too.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: When did you find her like this?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Just now, about twenty minutes ago.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What did you come to Rita's for?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Her parents are in the treatment area. It was her all alone here, making dinner for her mother and father. What were you doing here?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: I... I... She didn't come picking with us today, that's why! So I just came to see if something was wrong!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Liar! She said the harvest group wouldn't share anything with her! She hasn't gone with them for several days now!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: If you truly cared about that, you would've come much earlier, not just now!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Where's the food she picked today? Why isn't it in this room? Did you break in here and steal her food?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: I'm just trying to help my family survive too! There's not much food anywhere left at all!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: I didn't know... she'd resist so hard... I didn't know... and now she's in this state...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Victoria's nobles will not overlook us. The distress team we sent should have found a city by now!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: And even if that's true, my children won't be able to last until then.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: That doesn't call for robbing a young girl of her food! She collected it by her own efforts.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: This scalding on her palms was because out of fear of you stealing it, she directly tried to carry the boiling pot away, right?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The contusions on her arms were from you grabbing her, right?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The back of her head was you pushing her and knocking her against something, RIGHT?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: I didn't... mean to hurt her like this...

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Her mother and father are done for! Even if she survives, so what? Before long, she'll just be a... an orphan! Even if everything gets better, she can't live on alone!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: My children and I are still healthy! Surely our whole family surviving carries more weight than her.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Is that it? You'll weigh their lives...?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Then how about me? My life? How much weight do you see in me?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I've had a little hunch you've all been gawping at me and my Eulogy, whispering about who in the world I could be.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So be so kind as to tell me, how much weight do you see in this single life of mine?

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: M—Madam! You've treated us, saved us, some of us have guessed you might be a Victorian noble... out of all of us here, you're the most honorable...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Then shouldn't you be giving your food to me, making my survival easier?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Because I—for one—haven't eaten well in a very long time!

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: ...That's...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But you wouldn't be willing to give food to me, would you?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You don't follow any logic, or reason, or any just course of action. All you are is selfish.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I—despise—the selfish, and I'd let alone even the thought of aiding a robber.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: In light of you at the VERY least informing me about this, I'll give you one more chance—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Return the food, with not one bit missing! If you've eaten it, make up for it! Or else I guarantee, the distress group's caravan will have no place for you in it.

steps.name: Leithanian Refugee
steps.text: Yes... I understand, madam.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: *sigh*. So I have it in my nature to tell petrifying lies like that too. Whatever, as long as it had a use.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Malnutrition, fever, physical trauma, inflammation.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'll give this fever medication to Rita for now, seeing as it's prepared. If I don't have enough, I can pick some more in a bit to give to the patients in the treatment area.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: *whimper*... don't steal my Mama and Papa's porridge...!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita! It's me, Grace. I'm just borrowing your pot for the moment, decocting some herbs for you. No need to be scared.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Take this drink in a moment, and you'll feel a little better.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: My Mama and Papa's... food... got... stolen...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It's okay, your food will come back. Just trust in me for now, and get some rest.

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Mnn...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Here, I've already blown it cool it for you, Rita. Open your mouth a bit.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: That's great, Rita! There's a little spilling from your mouth. Let me wipe that for you.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It'll be effective soon. Just sleep here for a bit. I'll go fetch some other medicines for you!

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: Zzz... zzz...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Already asleep? That's some effective medicine. Just wait for me, now, I'll be right back.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It's pouring buckets now... so dark...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I need to move quick! If I'm any later, I won't be able to see it!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: My foot... ow...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I remember the herbs I was looking for were right near here... leaves like arrowheads, fine sawteeth on top. Ah! Is this it?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: There! All clean. Now to grind into a powder!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Why do I start swooning the moment I apply any force...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Come on, please, just hold on a little more!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Okay, and these herbals in matching proportion.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ah, there's not enough firewood!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Temperature... I need to collect more firewood.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ohh...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita. Rita. Don't be scared. I'll feed you some medicine now. It might be a tiny bit... hot.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Oh, I think I forgot to pick out the seeds... it might be very bitter, too.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I've already applied topical medication to you. This is for reducing your fever. Here, drink, and you'll be much better soon.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I won't let anything happen to you...

steps.name: Rita
steps.text: (Strained gulp)

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Heehee, good girl, Rita!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So dizzy... I can't keep... should—I rest for a moment...?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Rita... Rita... you have to...

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: She was like this when we found her, mumbling the name over and over.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: She's covered in mud, her ankle is injured, and she has minor Oripathy infection symptoms. Was she only recently infected?

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Oripathy infection is only one part of it. The major contributing factors to her fainting were starvation and extreme exhaustion.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Reports say she's been passed out for several days now. Some refugees say this young woman was protecting them. Without her efforts, hardly this many would have survived.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: The refugees regained capacity for labor after recovering, and were able to request treatment and a place to stay from Mr. Gurk of Leithanien. He required people to staff and safeguard that bizarre castle of his.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: These people's home was struck by severe Catastrophe. Going back seems unlikely at present, so most refugees have accepted this proposal. They're prepared to undergo treatment at Mr. Gurk's, and to wait for now to see if they should return home.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Only the reasonable grounds of allowing these refugees to return to their home country could convince any related nobles not to interfere.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: About the young girl named Rita. Her mother has already passed on. Fortunately, her handicapped father is still able to work.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: A Catastrophe Messenger in the vicinity mentioned Earthspirit on the Rhodes Island landship is an old acquaintance of Gurk's. I'll write her a letter asking for a favor, to see if this father and daughter can be admitted onto his estate.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: The young Vulpo lady was unorthodox enough to leave deep impressions on people, but plucking herbal medicine and understanding some clinical theory was all she had. No way of suppressing her own Oripathy.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: She's too simple about the task of aiding refugees. It would've cost her her life sooner or later if she was too reductive about it.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: In a moment, I want you to make contact with a nearby Messenger. There's two letters I want to send. One to Rhodes Island, and another to a place in Toron.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: I'm compelled to remind you, Victoria has nobles who want those refugees dead here to serve their vie over territory. So as to keep our motive secure, we cannot at this moment openly represent Rhodes Island.

a.text: ...Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Not to mention you slipped out of a Victorian medical seminar to come here. Your actions must be kept subdued. It'll be best you don't give even more issues the chance to form.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: Oh, I was in an academic seminar, huh. See, these past few days, I was under the impression I'd be participating in some wannabe Durins' wine-tasting.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: Heh. To some nobles, philanthropy is a trend, and a trend is as far as it goes. They weighed the pros and cons, and did something anyone could've seen coming from a mile off.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: She's too weak. If we don't immediately treat her, further illness will seize hold of her, and we'll see her Oripathy infection accelerate.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: Let her pass off as my assistant and get the best treatment Victoria has to offer.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: Yeah, no kidding, we're gonna keep our true identities a secret from her. You happy with that?

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Assistant? Why do I suspect you're thinking of having her by your side?

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: I'm no nanny. You ever seen me drop in from the Victorian skies on an umbrella?

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: Once she recovers, I'll contact a specialist place and get her on a course for medical Arts, and I've got other fish to fry in the meanwhile.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: If she wants to keep up her innocent little savior business, I'm not gonna write in to complain.

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: But as a doctor with Oripathy, she's got no choice. She can't keep playing the wild maverick forever. Bottom line, she needs to learn how to protect herself. How her own future spirals out is her business.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Suit yourself. *sigh*. I suppose once Scout's done with his mission, I'll be transferring to his squad anyway. Having a Victorian local by your side to keep an eye on you works out.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: I weep for that Vulpo...

steps.name: Razor-like Voice
steps.text: She's sure as hell a lot more confident than you when she treats people.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Hm. And her prescriptions when treating non-Oripathy patients are particularly effective.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: I think I see what it is.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Kindness, strength, honesty, a tender age yet already at such standards.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: You want to defend a possibility.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Yes, I'd... very much like to see how she does too. It's a shame I'll probably be on my way back to Rhodes Island before she wakes up.

a.text: Rhodes Island...?

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: Brave young Vulpo, do get better soon.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: There's still so many people waiting for you—I'll be waiting too, to see how you grow, what you become.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: But I suppose you probably can't hear me right now... hahah...

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: I want to witness your future too, young Vulpo.

steps.name: Warm Voice
steps.text: If we've been brought together, if we'll ever meet again in future, maybe at Rhodes Island, maybe in some other place somewhere...

a.text: Rhodes... Island...
Eulogy—
After coming aboard Rhodes Island, I never could find that warm voice again.
Lady Earthspirit and Mr. Gurk continued correspondence. Rita is currently... not doing well, per se, but at least she can eat her fill.
And I'm doing... very busily here at Rhodes Island. It's very fulfilling, too. I've been in the company of truly outstanding doctors and scholars, trying some major things without break.
Eulogy... thank you all, for forgiving the scene I made.
I'm sorry. I've...
Caught Oripathy.
I'm stood on this vast world, Oripathy stretching far and wide—
And I hope... there'll come a day of finality, from where I can see the light.
